children: India on Friday criticised the US decision to restrict a key green-card processing programme for major global and Indian IT firms, including Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro, saying the move fails to advance the shared ambitions of both nations, and dismissed US Vice President JD Vance's characterisation of foreign professionals as 'indentured servants' as entirely "unwarranted and deeply offensive."

As part of broader efforts to bring down the number of foreign workers in the US, the Trump administration suspended the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme for eight IT majors and launched probes into several universities, a decision that comes amid continuing strain in India-US ties.

The companies facing the action are Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Microsoft, Adobe, Capgemini and Cognizant. The PERM is widely considered as a pathway for permanent residency and citizenship in the US.
The US decision is expected to affect thousands of Indian technology professionals who rely on employer-sponsored green cards for permanent residency in the US after entering on H-1B visas.
In its reaction, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) , criticising the US move, at the same time said the PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme.

It said suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency and Green card process of eligible employees of the affected companies.

"It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US," the MEA said.

"This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries," it said.
New Delhi also took strong objection to Vance's remarks on foreign professionals serving in the US.

title: India slams US Green card suspension for IT firms, blasts Vance's 'indentured servants' remark
